organization: Health and Welfare Council of Long Island
program: Benefits enrollment and HEALI social-care network coordination

acceptance.evidence: givebetter-nyc-sixth-seventh-independent-acceptance.json: primary-source checks, independent reconstruction of every scenario, and explicit uncertainty review; accepted as conditional alpha modeling, not measured causal impact.

what: HWCLI helps Long Island residents enroll in benefits and coordinates the HEALI social-care network.
The health model covers additional insurance access and a narrowly discounted nutrition-services pathway in Nassau and Suffolk counties.
The central model implies about $50.2 million per10 NYC-MSA QALYs.
strengths: Clear Nassau/Suffolk service footprint inside the MSA.
An operating public-benefits and social-care infrastructure can connect otherwise missed residents to services.
The model separates recipient coordination credit, alternative help and marginal funding.
reservations: The 2025 report reproduces a financial activity statement labeled 2024, so forward cost is uncertain.
Network service counts are not unique improved-health beneficiaries.
No measured unrestricted-gift elasticity or recipient-specific utility effect establishes the central judgments.

sections.what:
HWCLI provides benefits navigation and leads HEALI. HEALI contracts with providers and coordinates services; eligible care is Medicaid-covered. Nassau and Suffolk are both in the defined MSA. [Network structure](https://healiny.org/about/)

The report records 4,891 insurance enrollments and 7,000 network nutrition services in 2025. These are distinct model inputs, not health outcomes. [2025 report](https://hwcli.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/06/FINAL-2025-HWCLI-ANNUAL-REPORT.pdf)
sections.monitoring: Track completed coverage, genuinely otherwise-uninsured months, distinct nutrition recipients and completed service intensity, plus pre/post utility with comparison groups. Do not count screenings, benefit dollars or referrals as QALYs. Oregon randomized evidence found improved mental health but no significant measured physical-health improvements at two years; our 0.01 annual utility assumption is an explicit transfer judgment, not a trial coefficient. [Original trial](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMsa1212321)
sections.qualitative:
Coordination may reduce language and administrative barriers, but providers, public insurers and other navigators remain active without a new gift. The network's own description confirms multiple independent partners and Medicaid financing; HWCLI cannot receive all network health credit. Unmodeled housing, maternal-health and advocacy outcomes are set net zero, not established absent. [HEALI](https://healiny.org/about/)

Retained benefits, grocery resources and private payments require targeted assessment; unknown is not zero.
sections.cost:
Signed household resources are assessed unknown and potentially material. The retained clinical reference uses 2.0528750000000002 MSA QALYs at $10,313,844 forward annual recipient cost. All six original worlds remain unchanged. This is not a complete combined valuation, zero-resource finding or empirical 90% health share.

The [2025 annual report](https://hwcli.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/06/FINAL-2025-HWCLI-ANNUAL-REPORT.pdf) verifies 6,586 individuals received SNAP application assistance, $10,000 corporate-sponsored grocery cards and a 28-patient nutrition pilot with grocery cards. The same report page8 records 512 CHA clients and families saving approximately ,166.03 in medical costs. Ana’s ,252 debt was eliminated through financial assistance. This is a direct household-resource anchor, but canceled bills need not equal cash otherwise paid. An optional one-time positive-only payment diagnostic applies explicit collection, retention, household/client incidence and additionality hypotheses; absent a household baseline and full costs it is not signed net welfare or a central numerical amendment. Direct food resources are also real mechanisms, not merely health proxies. However, applications are not awards; the sponsored historical distribution is not an additional future unrestricted-gift benefit; card allocations, realized SNAP amounts and net household counterfactuals are not identified. Seven thousand network nutrition services cannot be treated as unique households.

[HEALI](https://healiny.org/about/) states eligible support is Medicaid-covered. Existing funded networks and sponsor/partner delivery remain baseline. A numerical bridge requires deduplicated funding-responsive households, actual retained benefits and private-food or care payments displaced against alternatives, net baseline, finite duration and delay. Taxes, benefits withdrawn and full shopping, travel, recertification, administration and time burdens must be included independently of clinical response; positive overlap applies only to gains. Public reimbursement, retail meal value and institutional savings are not household cash. Broader resources remain unquantified, not absent.

Central cost is $10,313,844: twice $5,156,922 historical whole-recipient expense for forward SCN ramp-up. Health=.25×[4,891×.3×.01×.5 +7,000×.25×.5×.02×.5×.2×.5]=2.0528750000000002 MSA QALYs, or $50,240,974 per 10. The final 0.5 nutrition factor removes potential overlap with coverage utility. All causal conversion factors are judgments. For an illustrative $1,000 gift, whole-portfolio scaling corresponds to 0.474 historical enrollments and 0.679 network nutrition units before additionality/attribution adjustments; these are normalized activity equivalents, not promises or measured unit costs. No mortality benefit, perpetual benefit or public treatment savings is added. Partner and public medical costs are outside recipient cost.
sections.funding:
The original annual report lists $5,156,922 expenses, including $2,472,321 personnel/fringe and $2,684,601 nonpersonnel, in its activity statement labeled 2024 despite a 2025-financials heading. We preserve the statement year and do not treat this as an audited 2025 cost. Its balance-sheet/net-asset figures conflict internally and are not used for a reserve estimate. No three-year mean is established. [Financial page](https://hwcli.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/06/FINAL-2025-HWCLI-ANNUAL-REPORT.pdf)

An unrestricted gift is modeled as following the whole portfolio, with only 25% incremental capacity after substitute grants, public funding and reserves. Neither that fraction nor the forward multiplier is observed. The website has a donation link, but there is no verified restricted marginal offer. [Official site](https://hwcli.com/)

model.costScope: Whole-recipient 2024 reported activity expense times explicit forward-cost multiplier 2; not network-wide social cost. No expense denominator from older cost is silently paired with new ramp-up output.
model.geographicAttribution: g=1 for modeled Nassau/Suffolk pathways, both MSA member counties; no headquarters inference.
model.formula: Q=g*b*(E*a*u*t+N*d*c*v*s*k*z); cost=C*f; price10=10*cost/Q. z removes nutrition utility already captured in coverage term; mortality=0.
model.counterfactual: Existing Medicaid care, the SCN, partners and alternative enrollment help continue. Coverage additionality .3, nutrition alternative-care .5, HWCLI attribution .2 and funding .25 are separate judgments; no blanket public baseline credit.
model.attribution: Insurance term .3 credits genuinely additional coverage; network term .2 reserves 80% of incremental network health for delivery partners and other actors. Both multiplied by .25 capacity additionality of ordinary gifts. Nutrition utility multiplied by nonoverlap z=.5, separate from HWCLI causal share and financing additionality.
model.uncertainty: Very weak-confidence subjective scenarios; no recipient QALY trial. Cost-year mismatch, repeat service intensity and marginal public-finance substitution dominate.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional insured person-years and distinct sustained nutrition recipients; health utility limited to half a year; mortality credit zero.

sensitivity: Doubling the central forward multiplier from 2 to 4 doubles price; this explicitly tests 2025 ramp-up cost mismatch.
Setting b, additional coverage, or utility to zero removes their pathway benefit. Network attribution cannot be assumed 100%.
Other harms exceeding 2.0528750000000002 incremental QALYs erase central health; zero omitted-portfolio health is not a lower bound.
Nutrition nonoverlap z ranges0–1; central.5. Enrollment and nutrition records are not linked, so disjoint benefit is not presumed.
missingInputs: Original 2025 audited expense and pass-through accounting, resolving contradictory 2024-labeled annual report page.
Deduplicated network nutrition recipients, intensity and matched utility outcomes.
Unfunded marginal plan and unrestricted-gift allocation after Medicaid and grant reimbursement.
Independent enrollment counterfactual and effective covered months.

Unique gift-responsive CHA households, cash collections that would otherwise occur from reported bill relief, retained SNAP/food amounts, net household baseline, full burdens, finite payment timing and payer incidence.

incomeAssessment.rationale: The annual report verifies $277,166.03 of client medical-cost savings across 512 CHA community members, with a debt-elimination vignette, plus grocery cards and nutrition support. These are resource-output anchors, not automatically actual private payments avoided. A conditional collection fraction can translate debt relief, but household sharing, alternative collection and full net burdens remain unidentified.
directions: Retained SNAP and actual grocery-card consumption or displaced private food purchases; private insurance/care payments against existing alternatives.
Full shopping, travel, recertification, administration and opportunity costs independent of clinical response; taxes and withdrawn benefits.
Existing Medicaid reimbursement and corporate sponsorship remain baseline; public financing, partner delivery and household incidence are separate.
incomeAssessment.missing: Unique gift-responsive CHA households, cash collections that would otherwise occur from reported bill relief, retained SNAP/food amounts, net household baseline, full burdens, finite payment timing and payer incidence.

reference.scope: Optional one-time positive-only medical-payment transfer diagnostic, not central signed net resources. One household per CHA client, collection, retention, additionality and overlap are hypotheses; baseline and full costs unidentified. No clinical-response multiplier; no annual recurrence.
